This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, Digital Realty ACC10, matches an Inflect listing and a DataCenterMap listing, both whose own building code exactly matches this rows name, giving 21744 Sir Timothy Drive, Ashburn, VA, directly across the street from this operators ACC9 building also tracked in this registry.

reading.body:
Digital Realty's ACC10 facility in Ashburn sits within one of the densest data center clusters in the United States, part of a Northern Virginia campus that likely exceeds 600 megawatts of total IT load across multiple named buildings.

The concentration of facilities in Loudoun County reflects how data center operators consolidate operations geographically once infrastructure—power delivery, fiber routes, real estate zoning—reaches critical mass. Digital Realty acquired most of these Ashburn buildings through two major transactions that added legacy naming conventions still visible in facility registries: the 2017 merger with DuPont Fabros brought twelve facilities with "ACC" designations, while earlier acquisitions consolidated smaller operators. This pattern shows how the data center market consolidates through M&A rather than dispersal.

For AI infrastructure planning, the significance is spatial. Thousands of megawatts of compute are now geographically stacked in places like Northern Virginia, meaning power and cooling constraints at the regional grid level directly throttle AI scaling. A single county's data center density creates bottlenecks that are not visible in individual facility specs. This data does not reveal current power utilization, interconnection capacity, or local grid headroom at ACC10 specifically, only that it exists within an already-massive cluster.
